title: find-media run manifest
description: Summary written to games/<game>/.find-media/run_manifest.json as a find-media run progresses, across SCOPE → PLAN → SEARCH → STOCK → JUDGE → INSTALL. One entry per media slot. A slot is DONE when it has an installed pick AND a stocked shelf of options in the options store — the manifest records both, plus every candidate a gate killed, so a later audit can tell a thin source from a bad query. Two invariants this schema enforces by shape: correctness is recorded as BINARY gates and never as points (see references/scoring_rubric.md), and there is NO accept threshold — candidates are ranked and stocked, the human decides. Used for resume, for audit_mode (references/audit_mode.md), and for the cross-run source ranking in by_source.

mode.description: Run-level default option target: fill=6, wide=12, deep=18. Mode is a shelf depth, not a retry budget. Per-item overrides live in items[].mode.

skill_version.description: Version of find-media skill that produced this manifest

total.description: Slots in scope for this run

installed.description: Slots with a file on disk — the game works

stocked_only.description: Slots with options on the shelf but no install (rare; means every candidate failed the strip)

failed.description: Slots with neither an install nor a usable shelf

skipped.description: Already present on disk, or deduped against used_assets.jsonl

options_stocked.description: Total options posted across all slots. Divided by `installed`, this is the real shelf depth the human sees.

strip_kills.description: ANIMATED candidates (.webm/.mp4/.gif) that passed the thumbnail read and then failed frame-strip verification. Historically ~half (3 of 5, then 4 of 6, in two rounds). A run of animated slots where this is near zero means the strip was skipped, not that the candidates were good. Static slots (.jpg location/clothing) cannot be stripped and never contribute here.

file_path.description: TOML-declared path, verbatim. The key for the options store, the review store, and dedupe.

type.description: The game-review item type (references/game_review_api.md). Not the same field as an option's media_kind, whose only legal values are img and video.

tier.description: The tier tag scripts/tier_format_check.py gates on — t0 and t1 are legal there, not 'unknown_tier'.

discovered_by.description: Which list surfaced this slot. Recording it separates a future API coverage gap from a genuine miss — the portrait classes were exactly such a gap until 2026-07-27, and the API enumerates them now.

route.description: Primary search route for this slot. Names must match references/chrome_route.md — typically google_images (Chrome — the only search route) or manual (URL supplied by the human). A PornHub-hosted result is a VOCABULARY source only (its title and tags), never a download candidate — see references/media_sources.md — so it is not a retrieval route here.

option_target.description: Options this slot was supposed to stock. Compare against options_stocked to spot thin sources.

options_stocked.description: Options actually accepted by options/add for this file

status.description: installed = a file is on disk AND options are stocked; stocked_only = shelf exists but nothing survived to install; failed = neither

brief.description: Echo of the demand block from templates/scope_brief.md. Carried here so an audit can judge a pick without re-reading the beat prose.

intended_heat.description: The carrier that makes the beat land — eye contact, being used, power, squalor, exposure

pov_case.description: Decided at SCOPE, never at judging time. 'defect' when the meaning needs the partner's body seen; 'fine' when the power is her face and eyes at the lens.

gate_inputs.description: The CLOSED list Gate 3 checks against — bodies only. Replaced the free-form must_show/avoid lists on 2026-07-31: those were filled 'straight from the beat prose', so rooms entered them and began rejecting clips, which scoring_rubric.md forbids. A fixed set of named fields has nowhere for a room to hide. Note `setting` is absent here on purpose — it lives in `queries` and on the SETTING axis, and is never a gate.

direction.description: Only when the act is ambiguous about who does what to whom

queries.description: Per-source query slots, not a ranked ladder — the Google and PornHub dialects are opposite, so ranking them against each other is meaningless.

candidates_returned.description: Downloadable urls harvested. Zero for a PornHub-dialect query by construction — that dialect returns vocabulary, not candidates.

bare_word_pool.description: PornHub dialect only: result count for the rare word ALONE. A compound query whose count exceeds this had the rare word silently dropped. Recorded because the tag pool sizes the WORD's usefulness; the results themselves are read for titles and tags, never queued for download.

terms_discovered.description: Vocabulary learned during this slot (e.g. downblouse, dogging, back alley). Google result labels and URLs are the richest source. Worth persisting: the term is reusable across games, the clip is not.

options.description: Every candidate that reached the shelf or died on the way. Stocked options are what the human flips through in the review UI; killed ones stay here as evidence. Stocking happens ONCE, right after extraction and BEFORE judging, so most options land here unjudged (no gates, no scores) and that is correct — judging only ranks and installs.

option_id.description: Stable candidate id — e.g. porngif.co/8f31c2, or a hash of the URL for hosts without ids

url.description: Original CDN URL with the query string STRIPPED — the browser JS tool blocks results carrying query-string data, and options/add dedupes on exact URL. This stripping is also why a signed, time-limited, IP-locked PornHub media url can never be a candidate: the signature lives in the query string we drop.

page_url.description: Where the candidate was found, if different from the media URL

source.description: Host that served the media. Keys by_source. Characterised fetchable hosts: blovjob.com, cdn.nsfwgify.com, xgroovy.com, porngif.co, cdn.hardcoregify.com, cdn.xgifer.com, imagex1.sx.cdn.live (sex.com), flashingjungle.com, static-ca-cdn.eporner.com. Any other host is 'surfaced, not yet characterised' — record it and let by_source tell you what it is worth. *.phncdn.com must never appear here: PornHub is discovery-only.

media_kind.description: As posted to options/add — the two legal values, never 'image'. .gif → img (it previews as an ), .webm/.mp4 → video. The backend lowercases the field and defaults to img (api/v1/media_finder.py, options_add). The renderer picks

strip_path.description: Local frame-strip path. Absent on an animated candidate means the strip was never built — which means unverified, not clean. Absent on a static candidate is normal; a .jpg cannot be stripped.

gates.description: Correctness, recorded as BINARY gates. Act, position, people count, affect, cast, and POV-when-the-scene-requires-the-partner-visible are pass/fail — they may NEVER be scored, because points are how a correct-but-dead clip out-totals a flawed-but-alive one. A null on any gate means it does not apply to this beat (e.g. no finish is called for). Absent whole object = the option was stocked but never judged.

passed.description: False if ANY gate below failed. A false here ends the candidate; it is not a low score.

cast.description: Who may be on screen, per the TOML character definitions

act.description: The described act — his hand is not his cock

position.description: Kneeling vs standing, from-behind vs supine

count.description: The beat's declared people count, in EITHER direction — two when the beat says three fails, and so does three when it says two

affect.description: Right affect. Right-but-limp is not a gate failure; it scores low on HEAT.

extra_people.description: Nobody present the beat doesn't have

finish.description: Only when the beat calls for a finish and the loop must show it

pov.description: Only when the scene's meaning needs the partner's body seen — a slack or watching man cannot also be the camera. POV is fine, often stronger, when the power is her face; when it is not a failure it must not be penalized on any axis.

failed_gate.description: Which gate ended it. Null when passed=true.

reason.description: Slug matching scores.jsonl gate_reason — cast:*, act:*, position:*, count:*, affect:*, finish:*, pov:*. `wrong_setting` is NOT a valid reason: setting is scored, never gated.

scores.description: Per-axis scores from references/scoring_rubric.md. EXACTLY three axes — nothing about what is depicted is scoreable, that lives in `gates`. Present only for options that were actually judged.

heat.description: Dominant axis (60 when setting is load-bearing, 85 when it isn't). Does the intended_heat carrier read on screen, held ACROSS the loop? On SFW items this same slot holds the LIFE score — lived-in and specific vs a stock render of the concept.

setting.description: Weight 25 when the setting carries danger, secrecy, or squalor. When it does not, the axis is SKIPPED and recorded as null — never scored low. Scoring a disposable setting low is the bug that discarded hot clips.

craft.description: Weight 15: can you read what is happening? Resolution is not a gate and barely an axis — a 264px clip won. Corner watermarks cost nothing.

heat_band.description: Which HEAT band the evidence put it in — the frame strip for animated candidates, the contact sheet for static ones. Drives the dead-clip veto at install time: a top-ranked DEAD option is not installed, the best ALIVE or WORKING one is.

score_total.description: heat + setting + craft, out of 100. A rank key for the shelf — never a pass mark. No accept threshold exists.

verified.description: How this candidate was actually looked at. `strip` = frame strip (every ANIMATED finalist). `contact_sheet` = a static finalist, which is judged from the sheet because a .jpg cannot be stripped. `thumbnail` = stocked alternate, unproven — legitimate on the shelf, never for the install.

strip_verdict.description: Frame-strip verification for animated candidates (.webm/.mp4/.gif) — route-independent, and mandatory for every animated finalist. Thumbnails lie constantly: a 'cluttered back room blowjob' thumbnail whose loop was standing kissing, a 'dark outdoor' thumbnail whose loop was a bright daytime laundromat. `not_applicable` = static candidate. `not_run` = an unstripped stocked alternate, which is fine; on an installed animated pick it is a defect.

strip_notes.description: What the strip showed that the thumbnail hid. Required when strip_verdict=fail.

decision.description: The three real outcomes. installed = written to disk as the best-guess pick; stocked = on the shelf for the human, whether or not it was judged; gate_reject = a named gate failed. There is no score-based rejection and no bar — a low total ranks last, it does not eliminate.

reject_reason.description: Echo of gates.reason for the rejected candidates — e.g. count:1_man, affect:smiling_when_used, pov:partner_needed. Never a setting complaint.

installed.description: True for the one option written to disk via the grab/capture API

posted_to_store.description: Accepted by POST /api/v1/dev/media-finder/options/add. Deduped by exact URL, so a false here usually means a duplicate, not an error.

human_selection.description: Recorded after the human reviews the shelf. Null until then — the run does not wait on it. This is the only place the manifest learns whether the installed best-guess was actually right.

matched_installed_pick.description: False means the skill's pick lost to a stocked alternate — the signal worth mining across runs

review_status.description: From media-review/reviews, where `game` is a QUERY param — as it also is on media-finder's options/list (GET); the media-finder POST endpoints take it in the BODY. Re-send the note on every status POST; posting a status without it WIPES the note. One decision covers every canvas reusing the asset.

pool_all_dead.description: True when every gate-surviving option landed in the DEAD heat band. Install the best of them anyway — the game must render — and say so plainly in the report. This is a query problem, not a verdict, and it is the honest replacement for the old accept threshold: nothing is withheld from the human, the shelf is just flagged.

pool_note.description: Free text for what the shelf is actually like when it needs a caveat — e.g. 'thin: 4 options, all one host', 'all DEAD, re-query with an anti-studio modifier'. Surface it rather than silently dropping the slot; a named flaw beats a blank shelf.

by_source.description: Per-host yield, keyed by the `source` field on each option. This is the mechanism for empirically ranking the sites the Chrome route reaches — the fetchable corpus is nine hosts the old single-source route never saw, gathered across queries and each measured fetchable on clearnet with no signing and no expiry: blovjob.com, cdn.nsfwgify.com, xgroovy.com, porngif.co, cdn.hardcoregify.com, cdn.xgifer.com, imagex1.sx.cdn.live (sex.com), flashingjungle.com, static-ca-cdn.eporner.com. Accumulate it across runs; after a few games it tells you which hosts to read first, and it is where a newly-surfaced, not-yet-characterised host earns or loses its place.

strip_passed.description: Animated candidates that survived frame-strip verification — the honest quality signal

human_selected.description: Chosen by the human over the alternates. The only ground truth here.

hit_rate.description: strip_passed / candidates, over animated candidates only. Meaningless for a host that only ever served static images — leave it absent there.

by_tier.description: Per-tier outcome, keyed by tier (base, location, t0–t8). Reveals whether failures cluster at specific tiers — a t5 column of stocked_only means the query dialect is wrong for explicit beats, not that the run was unlucky.

strip_kill_rate.description: strip_kills / animated candidates evaluated at this tier
